discovery: Dynamical symmetries and supersymmetry in atomic nuclei: the interacting boson model and algebraic methods in many-body quantum physics
motivation: Francesco Iachello created the interacting boson model with the late Akito Arima. It showed that the collective spectra of heavy nuclei follow dynamical symmetries of the group U(6). The three limits, U(5), SU(3) and O(6), turned a bewildering variety of spectra into a small set of analytic classes. Iachello then proposed dynamical supersymmetry, which links the spectra of neighbouring even-even and odd-mass nuclei, and precise spectroscopy later confirmed this. The supersymmetric quartet around 196Au is the most striking case. He also introduced critical-point symmetries, E(5) and X(5), for shape phase transitions, and these too were observed experimentally. The same algebraic framework now describes molecular vibrations through the vibron model, as well as hadron spectra and quantum phase transitions in finite systems. His work is a rare case of abstract group theory making sharp, falsifiable predictions across disciplines, and it defined a generation of research worldwide.
